label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — resolved sink value is rememberMeKey derived from java.lang.Math.random() (line 88-89), which is a weak/predictable RNG. This value is used as a remember-me cookie value (line 118) and session attribute (line 121), constituting a real insecure randomness vulnerability for authentication/security tokens. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-FP — resolved sink values are rememberMe.getName() = "rememberMe" + testCaseNumber (testCaseNumber derived from class name, not user input) and rememberMe.getValue() = rememberMeKey (derived from Math.random(), not user-controlled). Neither source is attacker-controlled user input; they are server-generated values. Case TP driven by Alert 1.

evidence.note: Math.random() (insecure RNG) generates value converted to rememberMeKey via Double.toString().substring(2)
rememberMeKey (from insecure RNG) used as remember-me cookie value and session attribute — security-sensitive context
XSS sink prints rememberMe.getName() (server-derived cookie name) and rememberMe.getValue() (RNG-derived key), neither is user-controlled input
